answer: PoA identity verification binds each claimed node to a Wesolowski VDF: a fixed chain of sequential modular squarings must finish before its proof is accepted. An attacker simulating clones cannot shorten or merge these dependency chains; GPUs may run chains separately, but cannot parallelize one chain’s squarings, even across GPUs. This strict physical time bottleneck makes a lagoon of fabricated agents costly, while proofs cross the bridge to consensus and enforce the zenith deadline.
